title: Calculator
description: One memory register per user: exact u64 arithmetic with refusals, isolation between users, the get round trip, and the PostgreSQL store.
author: Claude (agent-authored explanation; review before relying on it)
exclusions: That the bearer token's principal is the real caller depends on the HMAC secret and is outside the proofs.
Tenant separation, SERIALIZABLE retries and idempotent replay are framework properties, not theorems of this app.
The real PostgreSQL server and driver are trusted to behave like the Lean model; the differential test is evidence, not proof.
Databases edited by hand, migrated or created with a different schema are outside the modeled histories.
Fidelity of Charon and Aeneas extraction, the Lean kernel and rustc are trusted.
Availability, latency and concurrency throughput are not covered.

nodes.title: Arithmetic results are exact
nodes.description: When `apply` succeeds, your new memory is exactly your old memory plus, minus, times or divided by the argument, computed on natural numbers. The same value is returned and written to your own memory.

nodes.title: Impossible operations are refused with the right reason
nodes.description: A result of 2^64 or more is refused as overflow, a result below zero as underflow, and division by zero as division_by_zero. A refusal carries no write.

nodes.title: Valid operations are accepted
nodes.description: If the true result of `memory op arg` is a natural number below 2^64, the kernel accepts the command and returns that result. It never refuses a computation the specification allows.

nodes.title: The kernel never crashes
nodes.description: For every caller, every stored state and every command, the kernel returns a reply or a refusal. No input makes it panic, overflow a machine integer or index out of bounds.

nodes.title: A command writes only your own memory
nodes.description: Whatever command you send, the row the kernel asks to write belongs to you. No command can produce a write to another user's memory.

nodes.title: Other users' memories are unchanged
nodes.description: After any successful command by one user is committed, every other user's memory reads exactly as before.

nodes.title: Get returns what your last command produced
nodes.description: After a successful set, apply or get is committed, a get by the same user returns that command's result.

nodes.title: Get only reads, and an unset memory reads as 0
nodes.description: A get always succeeds, writes nothing, and returns your stored value. A user who never stored anything reads 0.

nodes.title: The database holds exactly the computed memories
nodes.description: For the modeled PostgreSQL database, after any history of requests the tenant's rows are the rows of the memories the commits computed, and loading them decodes back to those memories, up to row order.

nodes.title: Rust arithmetic agrees with eval
nodes.description: For every operation and every pair of U64 values, `compute` succeeds without panicking. It returns Ok v exactly when `eval` gives v, and Err e exactly when `eval` refuses with e.

nodes.title: Multiplication overflow check
nodes.description: For b > 0, the Rust test `a > MAX / b` holds exactly when a * b is at least 2^64. This is the one nonlinear fact `compute_spec` needs.

nodes.title: Memory lookup agrees with memOf
nodes.description: The loop in `memory_of` always terminates without error and returns `memOf` of the vector's contents for that user.

nodes.title: transition never fails
nodes.description: For every principal, snapshot and command, `transition` returns `ok` of some result. In the extracted model every panic is an error, so this rules out panics.

nodes.title: apply computes eval on my memory
nodes.description: For an Apply command, `transition` succeeds. If it returns a value v, then `eval` on the caller's memory gives v and the write is the caller's row with v. If it returns an error e, `eval` gives the same error.

nodes.title: Writes target the caller
nodes.description: For every command, if `transition` returns Ok with a write, that row's user equals the caller's user.

nodes.title: Commit is an upsert
nodes.description: Assuming the memories vector has room for one more element, `apply` succeeds and its memories are unchanged for no write, or the old list with that user's row replaced or appended.

nodes.title: Every success reads or writes the result
nodes.description: For every command, a successful reply v either comes with no write and equals the caller's memory, or comes with a write of v to the caller's row.

nodes.title: Get reads memOf
nodes.description: A Get always returns Ok with no write and the value `memOf` gives for the caller.

nodes.title: Round trip through commit
nodes.description: Assuming room for one more row, a successful transition with reply v, and that `apply` committed its write into s', a Get by the same principal on s' returns v.

nodes.title: Isolation between users
nodes.description: Assuming room for one more row, a successful transition by a, and that `apply` committed its write into s', every user u different from a has the same `memOf` value in s' as in s.

nodes.title: A concrete round trip
nodes.description: On the empty snapshot, Alice's set of 5 commits and a following get returns 5. This shows the hypotheses of `get_after` can all hold at once.

nodes.title: SQL writes match the model
nodes.description: For every write set, `sql_writes` succeeds and its plan is the modeled table write `sqlA`: nothing for no write, one put for a memory.

nodes.title: Store holds what commits computed
nodes.description: For every database produced by a `Served` history, the tables hold the encoded memories, and every complete load decodes to a snapshot equivalent to them up to row order.

nodes.title: The same on PostgreSQL
nodes.description: Assuming a valid one-table schema and an integer tenant value, for every database produced by a `PgServed` history, the tenant's view holds the encoded memories and every load by the compiled SELECT decodes to them up to row order. This is the theorem `h5i app check` gates.

nodes.title: Subtracting 1 from an empty memory is refused
nodes.description: A concrete negative case: Alice's memory starts at 0, and Apply Sub 1 returns Err Underflow rather than wrapping around to 2^64 minus 1.

nodes.title: eval: the arithmetic we mean
nodes.description: The answer to `a op b` on natural numbers, or the reason there is none below 2^64: Overflow, Underflow or DivByZero.

nodes.title: memOf: a user's memory
nodes.description: The value of the first row for user u, or 0 when there is none.

nodes.title: Committing a write set
nodes.description: The memories after a commit: unchanged for no write, otherwise an upsert of the row keyed by user.

nodes.title: Table encoding
nodes.description: The rows of table 0 are the memories, encoded with `Memory.row`. No other table has rows.

nodes.title: The calculator as a store app
nodes.description: Packages the encoding, the table writes `sqlA`, the commit `step` and the empty initial state for the shared `H5iAppLib.Store` theorem.

nodes.title: A load by compiled SELECT
nodes.description: A Rows value counts as a load when the compiled SELECT for the tenant runs on the database and returns the same rows in some order.

nodes.title: Database produced by the server
nodes.description: The database starts empty and changes only by commits in which a loaded snapshot decodes and the `sql_writes` plan is executed. Databases changed by hand or by a migration are outside this set.

nodes.title: PostgreSQL history produced by the server
nodes.description: Like Served, over the PostgreSQL model with all tenants: this tenant's commits run the compiled SQL, and other tenants' statements are allowed but use a different tenant value.

nodes.title: Room for one more row
nodes.description: The memories vector is shorter than Usize.max, so appending a row cannot overflow its length. `apply_spec`, `get_after` and `others_unchanged` all take this hypothesis.

nodes.title: The command succeeded and was committed
nodes.description: `get_after` and `others_unchanged` hypothesize that `transition` returned Ok and that `apply` turned its write into the next snapshot. A refused command is outside their statement.

nodes.title: The PostgreSQL schema is the declared one
nodes.description: `pg_stored` assumes the table list is valid, has one table with the kernel's key lengths, and that the tenant value is an integer. Whether the deployed database has that schema is not proved.

nodes.title: HMAC token identifies the caller
nodes.description: The server turns a bearer token signed with H5I_APP_SECRET into a Principal. Every theorem takes the principal as given; that it is the real person depends on the secret staying secret.

nodes.title: JSON decoding
nodes.description: `decode_command` must turn the request body into the command the client meant. Since the theorems hold for all commands, a wrong decoding can only produce a command the client could have sent.

nodes.title: Tenant selection
nodes.description: The framework loads the snapshot of the caller's organization, chosen by `tenant`. The kernel theorems are about one snapshot; keeping tenants apart is enforced by the framework, not by these proofs.

nodes.title: Transaction engine
nodes.description: Each request runs load, transition, write and commit in one SERIALIZABLE transaction with retries, so a refusal commits nothing. This engine behavior is part of the framework's trusted contract.

nodes.title: Extraction and toolchain fidelity
nodes.description: The theorems are about the Lean that Charon and Aeneas produced from the kernel. That this matches the compiled Rust, and that Lean and rustc are sound, is trusted.

nodes.title: Retries with Idempotency-Key
nodes.description: A retried request with the same key replays the stored reply instead of running again. This is a framework property, not one of these theorems.

nodes.title: Deployment configuration
nodes.description: The database URL, the signing secret, the listen address and the schema installation come from the environment at startup. Nothing in the proofs covers them.

nodes.title: POST /rpc route
nodes.description: The axum router merges the framework's ready-made /rpc route with a /healthz probe.

nodes.title: JSON API codec
nodes.description: Decodes the request into a Command, encodes a Reply as {"value": v}, and maps each refusal to a 422 error code.

nodes.title: Kernel trait wiring
nodes.description: Points the framework at the kernel's `transition` and `apply` without adding any decision.

nodes.title: transition
nodes.description: The whole application logic: Set writes the value, Apply reads the caller's memory and runs `compute`, Get reads without writing.

nodes.title: compute
nodes.description: The checked u64 arithmetic with explicit overflow, underflow and division by zero tests. `h5i-app.toml` declares the underflow_boundary mutant against the Sub test.

nodes.title: memory_of
nodes.description: A while loop over the memories that returns the first value for the user, or 0.

nodes.title: apply (commit)
nodes.description: Clones the snapshot and puts the written row with the generated `Memory::put`, which replaces the user's row or appends it.

nodes.title: sql_writes
nodes.description: Turns a write set into the table writes the server executes: one put for a memory, nothing otherwise.

nodes.title: memories table schema
nodes.description: `schema!` declares the Memory row keyed by user and generates the row operations, SQL writes, decoder and the server's table mapping.

nodes.title: CalcStore load and write
nodes.description: Loads a tenant's rows with the generated schema loader and writes the rows that `sql_writes` returns.

nodes.title: Differential PostgreSQL test
nodes.description: Runs 300 random commands through the PostgreSQL engine and the in-memory engine that calls `apply`, and compares replies and final state. It is a test, not a proof, and skips without a test database.
